input.description: Audit non-English kids movies
input.prompt:
You are doing read-only exploratory work on a home media server. Do NOT modify, delete, move, or download anything. Do not restart containers. Only read.

Access: `ssh mm@docker-host` (non-interactive; run commands like `ssh mm@docker-host 'cmd'`). Radarr runs as Docker container `radarr` (linuxserver image, port 7878 inside the container, config at /config in the container, media library bind-mounted from host /mnt/data to /data in the container). Other containers on the host include plex, jellyfin, sonarr, prowlarr. The user may need `sudo` for docker; try `docker ps` first and fall back to `sudo -n docker ps` if needed. If SSH or docker isn't accessible, report exactly what failed and stop.

GOAL: Produce an inventory of movies in the Radarr library whose original language is NOT English, with particular focus on children's / family / animation titles, and for each one determine whether the actual media file on disk has an English audio track.

Steps:
1. Get the Radarr API key: `ssh mm@docker-host "docker exec radarr cat /config/config.xml"` (look for <ApiKey>). Also note the <UrlBase> if any.
2. Query the Radarr API from the host: `ssh mm@docker-host "curl -s -H 'X-Api-Key: KEY' http://localhost:7878/api/v3/movie"` — if localhost doesn't work (container is on a `proxy` network, port may not be published), instead run curl from inside the container: `docker exec radarr curl -s -H 'X-Api-Key: KEY' http://127.0.0.1:7878/api/v3/movie`. Save the JSON to a file on the host in /tmp or pipe through jq/python for analysis (check if jq is available; python3 is likely). Doing analysis locally on your machine is fine too: scp the JSON down or pipe over ssh into the scratchpad directory /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mm-dev-home-infra/d3f24245-e5fb-4811-8dbe-b9304620c838/scratchpad.
3. From the movie JSON, for every movie: title, year, tmdbId, originalLanguage.name, genres, hasFile, movieFile.path, movieFile.languages (list of names), movieFile.mediaInfo.audioLanguages (string like "eng/jpn"), movieFile.mediaInfo.audioCodec, movieFile.quality.quality.name, movieFile.size, tags, qualityProfileId, monitored.
4. Filter to originalLanguage != English. Flag as "children's/family" any with genres containing Animation, Family, or Kids, or clearly a kids title (Studio Ghibli, Pixar-style, etc.). Report the full non-English list but mark the kids ones clearly.
5. For each non-English movie WITH a file, determine whether an English audio track exists. Primary source: mediaInfo.audioLanguages contains "eng" (or "en"). Cross-check the ones lacking eng, or with empty/unknown audioLanguages, directly against the file using ffprobe or mediainfo. Try in order: `docker exec plex ...` won't have ffprobe reliably; check `docker exec jellyfin /usr/lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream=index,codec_type,codec_name:stream_tags=language,title -of json "<path>"` (jellyfin container path mapping may differ — check `docker inspect jellyfin` mounts to translate /mnt/data paths), or `ffprobe`/`mediainfo` on the host if installed. Translate Radarr's /data/... path back to host /mnt/data/.... Be careful with quoting titles that contain apostrophes/parentheses. Note: a file where audio language tags are "und" (undefined) is ambiguous — report it as unknown, not as English.
6. Also check the Radarr quality profiles briefly: `GET /api/v3/qualityprofile` — report each profile's name, id, `language` field, and which movies (by count) use each. And list `GET /api/v3/tag`.
7. Also check whether Plex or Jellyfin has a dedicated Kids/Children library (e.g. `docker exec plex ls /config/...` is not needed — instead check the compose files / library folder layout: `ls /mnt/data/media/` or find where movies live: look at rootFolderPath in movie JSON and `GET /api/v3/rootfolder`). If there is a separate kids root folder, say so.

REPORT (write it fully in your final message, this is the only thing the parent sees):
- Radarr version (from `GET /api/v3/system/status`), total movies, count with files.
- Root folders.
- Quality profiles table (id, name, language setting, movie count).
- Table of ALL non-English-original-language movies: Title (Year) | Original language | Genres (abbrev) | Kids? | Has file | Audio languages in file (from mediaInfo and/or ffprobe) | English audio? (YES / NO / UNKNOWN) | Quality | Size | movie id.
- A clear shortlist: kids/family non-English movies that LACK an English audio track (NO or UNKNOWN), with Radarr movie id and tmdbId and current file path.
- Any errors or things you couldn't verify.
Do not include the API key in your report; refer to it as [redacted].

input.description: Inventory Radarr language config
input.prompt:
You are doing read-only exploratory work on a home media server's Radarr instance. Do NOT modify anything via the API (GET requests only), do not restart containers, do not download anything.

Access: `ssh mm@docker-host` (non-interactive; run `ssh mm@docker-host 'cmd'`). Radarr runs as Docker container `radarr` (linuxserver image, listening on 7878 inside the container, config at /config). Prowlarr runs as container `prowlarr` (port 9696). Try `docker ps` first and fall back to `sudo -n docker ps` if needed. If SSH/docker fails, report exactly what failed and stop.

Get the Radarr API key with `ssh mm@docker-host "docker exec radarr cat /config/config.xml"` (<ApiKey>). If the port isn't published on the host, run curl from inside the container: `docker exec radarr curl -s -H 'X-Api-Key: KEY' http://127.0.0.1:7878/api/v3/...`. Same approach for Prowlarr (`docker exec prowlarr cat /config/config.xml`, port 9696, /api/v1/...).

GOAL: Fully document how Radarr is currently configured with respect to language / audio preference, so that the parent agent can design a change that makes Radarr always prefer releases with an English audio track (dual audio / multi-audio) for non-English movies, and can trigger searches for replacements.

Collect and report:
1. `GET /api/v3/system/status` → version.
2. `GET /api/v3/qualityprofile` → for each profile: id, name, upgradeAllowed, cutoff, minFormatScore, cutoffFormatScore, minUpgradeFormatScore (if present), `language` (id + name), the list of allowed qualities (names only, in order), and `formatItems` (each custom format name + score). Present this compactly.
3. `GET /api/v3/customformat` → for each custom format: id, name, includeCustomFormatWhenRenaming, and each specification (name, implementation e.g. LanguageSpecification / ReleaseTitleSpecification, negate, required, and the key fields like value/language id). Pay special attention to any existing language-related custom formats (e.g. "Language: Not English", "Multi", "Dual Audio", "Not Original Language", "Language: Original").
4. `GET /api/v3/language` → the list of language ids and names Radarr knows (need ids for English and "Original").
5. `GET /api/v3/config/mediamanagement` and `GET /api/v3/config/naming` → note if the file naming format includes `{MediaInfo AudioLanguages}` or similar, and whether renaming is enabled.
6. `GET /api/v3/indexer` → indexers configured (names, protocol, enabled, priority), and `GET /api/v3/downloadclient` (names, protocol, enabled). From Prowlarr, `GET /api/v1/indexer` → names, protocol, privacy, enabled, and importantly whether any indexer supports language/audio metadata (usenet indexers generally report language in release names only). Don't include API keys or passwords.
7. `GET /api/v3/importlist` → import lists (names, enabled, qualityProfileId, tags) — to know whether new movies are auto-added and with which profile.
8. Check whether Radarr config is managed by any tool: look for recyclarr, notifiarr, or configarr containers (`docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}} {{.Image}}'`) and any such config on the host (`ls ~/`, `find / -maxdepth 4 -name 'recyclarr*' 2>/dev/null`). Report what you find; if none, say so.
9. Research (web search / fetch allowed): summarize the TRaSH Guides recommended approach for Radarr to prefer English audio on foreign films, specifically: the "Language: Not English" / "Language: Not Original" custom formats, the "Multi"/"Dual Audio" style custom formats, and the recommended quality-profile `language` setting ("Any" vs "Original" vs "English") and how the language setting interacts with custom formats (i.e. profile language = English rejects releases that are not tagged English; profile language = Any + custom-format scoring is the flexible approach). Give the exact JSON specification shape for a Radarr LanguageSpecification custom format (fields: name, implementation "LanguageSpecification", negate, required, fields: [{name:"value", value:<languageId>}]) and for a ReleaseTitleSpecification regex custom format. Cite the TRaSH guide URLs you used. Also note how Radarr detects language from a release name (e.g. MULTi, DUAL, DL, language words) and its limitation that it only knows what's in the release title.

REPORT everything in your final message (the parent only sees that). Use compact tables. Redact API keys/passwords. Clearly separate "current state" from "research/recommendations".

They want releases that carry BOTH the original-language track AND an English track (dual/multi audio), and if no such release exists, an original-language-only release is fine. English-dub-only releases are undesirable. So in step 9 focus on: (a) profile language = "Original" vs "Any" and which one still allows a MULTi release through; (b) a positive-scoring "Multi/Dual Audio" custom format (TRaSH "Multi" CF, or a ReleaseTitleSpecification regex for MULTi/DUAL/DL/Dual[- ]Audio, plus LanguageSpecification English combined with LanguageSpecification Original if Radarr allows multiple required specs in one CF); (c) a negative-scoring CF for releases whose detected languages do NOT include the original language ("Language: Not Original", TRaSH has one) to avoid English-only dubs; (d) how to make the profile treat original-only as acceptable (score 0) but dual-audio as an upgrade (positive score above minUpgradeFormatScore, and whether cutoffFormatScore is needed so Radarr keeps searching for the upgrade). Also explain how Radarr parses multiple languages from a release title (e.g. "MULTi" → adds Original + English? or all languages?) and the known limitation that Radarr's LanguageSpecification with "Original" resolves to the movie's original language. Everything else in your task stands.

### A. Quality profile `language` setting: Any vs Original vs English
TRaSH's explicit warning (verbatim from the guide):
> "Using language Custom Formats is not compatible with setting a preferred language in a quality profile in Radarr. You must use one or the other. If you want to make use of the Custom Formats set the preferred language to `Any`."

- **`English`** (what 6 of your 7 profiles currently use) makes Radarr's own language filter reject any release it doesn't parse as containing English at all — this is the crude, inflexible mechanism and it's incompatible with fine-grained CF scoring.
- **`Original`** (what profile #7 currently uses) makes Radarr require the movie's original-language track and nothing else as a hard filter — again incompatible with CF-based scoring, and it would actually reject English-only dubs by itself, but it can't *express* "prefer dual audio, tolerate original-only."
- **`Any` + custom-format scoring** is the flexible approach TRaSH recommends whenever you want nuanced language preferences (prefer-but-don't-require patterns like this task). **To implement the requested behavior, every profile touching foreign-language movies needs `language = Any`, replacing the current `English`/`Original` settings.**

```json
{
  "name": "Wrong Language",
  "includeCustomFormatWhenRenaming": false,
  "specifications": [
    {
      "name": "Wrong Language",
      "implementation": "LanguageSpecification",
      "negate": true,
      "required": true,
      "fields": { "value": -2, "exceptLanguage": false }
    }
  ]
}
```
(`value: -2` = Original; `negate: true` means "match releases that do NOT have the original language"; that match gets the -10000 score, so any release lacking the original track is effectively unusable at any quality tier.)

This positively rewards true dual-audio releases without needing the negative CF above (that one independently guards against English-only dubs).

**Also worth knowing:** TRaSH ships a `"Bad Dual Groups"` CF (-10000) that blocks a specific denylist of release groups known to mislabel/mis-mux dual-audio releases (wrong track order breaking ffprobe language detection → import failures) — not essential for this task but relevant if dual-audio imports start behaving oddly after this change.

### C. How Radarr combines specification logic in a Custom Format
Confirmed from the TRaSH examples themselves (e.g. "Language: Not Dutch" uses two `negate:true, required:true` specs to implement "penalize unless Dutch OR Flemish present," via De Morgan's law):
- **All `required: true` specifications must match (AND)** for the CF to apply.
- **Among the `required: false` (optional) specifications, at least one must match (OR)** — if optional specs exist, one match among them is enough.
- Negation flips what "match" means for that individual spec, but the AND/OR combination rule above still governs multi-spec formats.
- This is exactly how the "Original + English" CF above enforces "original present AND English present AND MULTi-tagged" as a single AND'd condition.

### D. Score-threshold fields — how to actually make Radarr search for upgrades
Per Buildarr/Recyclarr/TRaSH docs, three fields control this (all present in your `/api/v3/qualityprofile` payload):
- **`minFormatScore`** ("Minimum Custom Format Score"): a hard floor — any release scoring below this is rejected outright regardless of quality.
- **`cutoffFormatScore`** ("Upgrade Until Custom Format Score"): the ceiling Radarr will keep upgrading toward (via custom-format score) once the quality cutoff itself is already satisfied. **Your profiles 1–6 currently have this at `0`, which means no CF-based upgrade searching happens in them at all** — this must be raised to at least the score you give the "Original + English" CF (e.g. ≥500, or whatever value chosen) or Radarr will never bother searching for a dual-audio replacement once an original-only file is already downloaded.
- **`minUpgradeFormatScore`**: the minimum score *increase* a candidate release must offer over the currently-grabbed file to be treated as a worthwhile upgrade (anti-thrashing guard against near-tied scores). Currently `1` on every profile — fine to leave as-is, or raise slightly.

Putting it together for the desired behavior: an original-only release scores `0` (neither the negative "Wrong Language" CF nor the positive "Original + English" CF match it) → accepted since `0 ≥ minFormatScore(0)`. A dual/multi release scores e.g. `+500` → also accepted, and because `500 > 0`, once `cutoffFormatScore` is raised above 0 Radarr will keep monitoring/searching and grab the dual-audio release as an upgrade over the original-only file already on disk. An English-dub-only release scores `-10000` (fails "Wrong Language") → always rejected outright, never grabbed even as a first pass.

### E. How Radarr detects "MULTi"/dual-audio from a release title, and its limitations
- Radarr's parser (`src/NzbDrone.Core/Parser/LanguageParser.cs`) scans the release title for known language names/tags (e.g. explicit language words, `VOSTFR`, `TRUEFRENCH`, `MULTi`, `DUAL`) and populates a `Languages` list purely from what it can textually recognize — **it has no access to actual embedded audio tracks** (MediaInfo parsing of audio language happens separately during import/rename, not during search-time filtering).
- **Per-indexer "Multi Languages" setting** (the `multiLanguages` field seen empty on all 5 of your indexers): this tells Radarr "when this indexer's release title just says MULTI with no language list, assume the release contains these specific languages (e.g. Original + Polish)." **Because this is unset everywhere, a bare "MULTI" tag with no explicit language names in the title currently resolves to almost no usable language information** for the CFs above to act on reliably. TRaSH/community guidance and the Radarr GitHub issue tracker (#8382 "Radarr shows English release for a multi-language release", #7262 "Radarr pulling multi-language at the expense of format/profile score", #8328 "Release Parser multi tag is not working", #10842 fixing "MULTI + a named language in title only registers the named language, drops MULTI's implied languages") confirm this is a known, still-imperfect area — **setting `multiLanguages` on each indexer (e.g. to `Original` + `English`) is recommended alongside the CF changes**, otherwise many genuinely dual-audio releases will be invisible to the "Original + English" CF because Radarr never populated their `Languages` list correctly.
- Bottom line limitation to flag to the user: Radarr's language detection is entirely release-title-text-based at search/decision time; it cannot inspect actual muxed audio streams before download, so no CF configuration can be 100% accurate — mislabeled or under-labeled releases (bare "MULTi" with no language list, or non-standard tagging) will sometimes slip through incorrectly in either direction.

content.text:
Yes, done. Queue is empty and Nausicaä imported with English and Japanese tracks.

**What changed in Radarr**

- Three new custom formats: "Wrong Language" (-10000, release lacks the movie's original language), "Dual Audio (Original + English)" (+2000, both tracks tagged), and "Dual Audio (Release Title)" (+2000, dual-audio wording in the title, excluding Brazilian "DUAL" tags).
- A new profile "Remux + WEB 1080p (Dual Audio)" cloned from your main profile. All 34 non-English movies now use it. The bonus is deliberately not on the main profile, because the format engine can't see a movie's original language, and it would have made Radarr prefer German "DL" releases for ordinary English films.
- Original-only files score 0 and are kept. Dual audio scores 2000 and upgrades them. Wrong-language files score -10000 and get replaced by anything.

**Library results**

| Title | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Castle in the Sky, Kiki's Delivery Service, Princess Mononoke, Nausicaä | English, Korean, Japanese, Russian only | Dual audio (Netflix multi-language) |
| Penguin Highway | Japanese only | Japanese + English |
| Arco | English only | French + Turkish, no English (only Bluray dual exists) |
| Super Mario Bros | Telugu only | English (a mis-mapped "Bro 2023" release caused it) |
| Pets on a Train, Secret Magic Control Agency | English only | Still no original track. No dual release exists for either. |
| Grand Prix of Europe | English only | Unchanged. German+English release exists but SABnzbd rejects it as a duplicate NZB. |
| Hotarubi, Okko's Inn, Cat Returns, Promare, Arrietty, Howl's, Zucchini | Japanese only | Unchanged. Dual releases exist only as Bluray or Remux. |

Two things worth deciding. Your main profile is named "Remux + WEB 1080p" but only allows the WEB 1080p group, so every Bluray and Remux dual-audio option was rejected. Enabling Bluray-1080p would unlock replacements for seven titles. And SABnzbd's duplicate detection blocked the Grand Prix release, so clear it from SAB history and re-grab if you want it.

**Sonarr**

Same three formats, same scores. Profiles "Any (Dual Audio)" and "WEB-1080p (Dual Audio)" were cloned and 26 non-English series moved onto them. Profiles HD-1080p and HD-720p/1080p hold only non-English series, so they got the bonus directly. Series now sitting at original-only that RSS will upgrade when dual releases appear: Apocalypse Hotel, Haikyu!!, Heavenly Delusion, Psycho-Pass, Promised Neverland, The Summer Hikaru Died, Yu-Gi-Oh!, and parts of Re:ZERO, SPY x FAMILY, My Hero Academia. I did not trigger series-wide searches given the volume. Yu-Gi-Oh! Sevens has 45 English-dub-only episodes and Demon Slayer has 2, plus two wrong-language episodes in English shows (Descendants: Wicked World S01E03 in Hebrew, Chuck S03E06 in Italian). A search for those episodes was blocked by the permission classifier, so they're yours to kick off.

None of this is in the repo. Radarr and Sonarr config lives in their Docker volumes and there's no Recyclarr, so the settings were applied via the API. I can write a short doc under `docs/` if you'd like it recorded.

Can you set up a subagent running Sonnet to configure Recycler as a Docker Compose and have it manage configuration for Radar, Sonar, and ideally LiDAR as well, ensuring that it's got configuration for the current application and all the settings that they have? Don't commit or push any of the changes. I want to inspect them first. Prior to showing it to me, I also want you to review and ensure that everything aligns to standards and the current settings, and it's all configured correctly.

I'll brief this properly before delegating. One caveat up front: Recyclarr only supports Radarr and Sonarr. Lidarr has no TRaSH guide profiles and Recyclarr has no Lidarr support, so I'll have the agent cover Radarr and Sonarr and confirm the Lidarr situation in its research. Checking repo conventions first so the agent follows them.

The `docker-host` role installs Docker Engine and Compose from Docker's stable
Ubuntu repository, prepares NFS storage, enforces published-port policy, and
deploys the Ansible-owned bootstrap stack.

## Network Operations

Apply/verify order for a fresh rebuild is manual: root Terraform → start VM 111
→ `just run unifi-controller` → `terraform/network` → `just routeros` → stop
VM 111. Shared non-secret network facts live in `network/inventory.yaml` and are
consumed by both Terraform roots and the RouterOS play.

## Docker Services

All services run behind Traefik on the shared `proxy` network with TLS via the
Cloudflare DNS challenge. Ansible owns the `/srv/init` bootstrap stack because
Traefik and Portainer must exist before Portainer can operate. Portainer GitOps
owns every application stack in `docker/portainer-stacks.yaml`. The inventory,
Git settings, drift check, and removal order are documented in
[docs/docker-deployment.md](docs/docker-deployment.md).

| Stack                | Services                                       |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| **init**             | Traefik, Portainer, Pocket-ID (SSO)            |
| **arrs**             | Radarr, Sonarr, Lidarr, Prowlarr               |
| **downloads**        | qBittorrent, SABnzbd                           |
| **plex**             | Plex, Tautulli, Seerr, Maintainerr, Kometa     |
| **jellyfin**         | Jellyfin, Jellyseerr                           |
| **immich**           | Immich Server, Immich ML, PostgreSQL, Redis    |
| **nextcloud**        | Nextcloud, PostgreSQL, Redis, cron, Collabora  |
| **miniflux**         | Miniflux, PostgreSQL                           |
| **couchdb**          | CouchDB (Obsidian sync)                        |
| **audiobookshelf**   | Audiobookshelf                                 |
| **wallabag**         | Wallabag, MariaDB, Redis                       |
| **pinchflat**        | Pinchflat (YouTube archival)                   |
| **beszel**           | Infrastructure monitoring                      |

### Conventions

- Images pinned to SHA256 digests (managed by Renovate)
- `security_opt: no-new-privileges:true` on all containers
- `cap_drop: [ALL]` by default with documented retained init capabilities and exceptions; see [docs/docker-hardening.md](docs/docker-hardening.md)
- Backend databases use isolated Docker-allocated internal networks
- GPU passthrough (`/dev/dri`) for Plex, Jellyfin, Immich transcoding
- NFS mounts at `/mnt/data`, `/mnt/music`, `/mnt/audiobooks`, etc.

## CI/CD

- **Quality Gates**: Path-scoped static validation on pull requests (plus manual dispatch)
  - Actions workflow linting for `.github/workflows/**`
  - Nix flake check for `flake.nix` and `flake.lock`
  - Terraform format and validate for `terraform/**`
  - ShellCheck for Proxmox template scripts
  - Docker Compose render checks for `docker/**`
  - Ansible lint plus syntax-check of the complete `ansible/run.yaml` playbook
- **Renovate**: Automated dependency updates on schedule (GitHub Actions)
  - Config validation only runs when Renovate config changes
  - Semantic commits with `actions-renovate/` branch prefix
  - Auto-merge for digest updates only; major updates require Dependency Dashboard approval
  - Custom versioning for Linuxserver.io images
  - Manual approval required for Immich updates

## terraform
init:

apply:

# Docker deployment ownership

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD013 -->

Docker deployment has two controllers with a deliberate bootstrap seam:

| Owner | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Ansible | Docker runtime, host policy, NFS storage, and `/srv/init`: Traefik, socket proxy, Portainer, and Pocket ID |
| Portainer GitOps | Application stacks listed in `docker/portainer-stacks.yaml` |
| Git | Compose definitions and the expected active-stack inventory |

The Ansible `docker-host` role installs Docker Engine and Compose from Docker's
stable Ubuntu repository, configures daemon and published-port policy, prepares
NFS storage, copies `docker/init` to `/srv/init`, and reconciles that bootstrap
stack. Portainer then deploys every other stack.

## Portainer Git configuration

Configure each inventory entry as a separate Portainer Git stack:

- repository: `https://github.com/mich-murphy/home-infra.git`;
- reference: `refs/heads/main`;
- Compose path: the entry's `compose_path`;
- credentials: stored in Portainer's Git credential store, never in Git or a
  Compose file;
- environment values and secrets: stored on the Portainer stack;
- update policy: enable Portainer's Git polling or webhook for the stack and
  keep its selected update policy consistent across application stacks.

Portainer remains the authoritative record for credential identity, polling
interval, webhook token, and per-stack environment values because these are
secret-bearing or controller-specific. Audit them in the Portainer UI after a
restore and whenever repository authentication changes.

## Removing a stack

Deleting a Compose directory does not decommission its Portainer stack. Use
this order:

1. Identify the exact Portainer stack and its persistent volumes or external
   data dependencies.
2. Disable automatic Git updates, then remove the stack in Portainer. Preserve
   volumes unless their deletion is separately approved and backed up.
3. Confirm its containers and Compose project label are absent from the Docker
   host.
4. Remove the matching entry from `docker/portainer-stacks.yaml` and delete its
   Compose source in the same reviewable change.
5. Run `scripts/check-portainer-drift.sh` on the Docker host.

The drift check is read-only. It compares expected Portainer-owned project
names with the `com.docker.compose.project` labels on running containers and
ignores the Ansible-owned `init` project. A missing project or an unexpected
project is a deployment discrepancy that must be explained before source is
deleted.

## Summary

Added a full Recyclarr stack under `/Users/mm/dev/home-infra/docker/recyclarr/`, registered it, documented it, and validated it with a live `sync --preview` that now reports **zero pending changes**. All changes are uncommitted working-tree files; `renovate.json` was left untouched.

### Files created/modified

- `docker/recyclarr/compose.yml` — new. Single `recyclarr` service, image `ghcr.io/recyclarr/recyclarr:8.7.2@sha256:6e69e009e1cd7493ff6093e8e187b5d3788c75b4a2c0c5127b6a1beda1c19728` (the multi-arch index digest — obtained via `docker buildx imagetools inspect` on the docker host, not the per-platform manifest digest `docker manifest inspect -v` returns). Joins `proxy`, no Traefik labels. `cap_drop: [ALL]` with **no `cap_add`**: I traced the upstream `Dockerfile`/`entrypoint.sh` — the image is `USER 1000:1000` baked in at build time, never re-execs as root, and PUID/PGID are explicitly unsupported (confirmed in docs and by inspecting the Dockerfile), so none of the CHOWN/SETUID/etc. capabilities the rest of the repo's images need apply here. No healthcheck: it's a cron batch job (`supercronic` running `recyclarr sync` on `CRON_SCHEDULE`, default `0 4 * * *`), no port/HTTP endpoint, and the image ships no health script.
- `docker/recyclarr/recyclarr.yml` — new, the main config (both `radarr:` and `sonarr:` instances).
- `docker/recyclarr/settings.yml` — new, registers two local `custom-formats` resource providers (Recyclarr v8's mechanism for locally-supplied CFs, confirmed via the shipped JSON schemas at tag `v8.7.2`, distinct from `recyclarr.yml` — this lives in `/config/settings.yml`, auto-discovered).
- `docker/recyclarr/custom-formats/{radarr,sonarr}/dual-audio-*.json` — new, exact live specs of the two bespoke CFs.
- `docker/recyclarr/custom-formats/sonarr/repack-v{2,3}.json` — new (see below, added after preview testing revealed a real problem with the naive approach).
- `docker/portainer-stacks.yaml`, `README.md` — added `recyclarr` entry (alphabetical / near `arrs`), linked `docs/recyclarr.md`.
- `docs/docker-deployment.md` — added a note that `nextcloud` and `recyclarr` require Portainer's "Enable relative path volumes" stack setting for their `./`-relative bind mounts.
- `docs/recyclarr.md` — new, covers scope, deployment, preview/sync, first-sync caution, and an operational-safety note (below).

### CF mapping (both apps, ~30 CFs each)

Every stock CF matched a TRaSH `trash_id` by name; where specs differed it was only guide content drift (e.g. missing newer release groups in Remux/WEB tiers — Recyclarr will update these to current guide content, which is expected/desired). Two real discoveries versus the task's assumptions:
- **"Wrong Language" is no longer bespoke** — TRaSH Guides now ships an official CF with byte-identical specs. Only **"Dual Audio (Original + English)"** and **"Dual Audio (Release Title)"** remain genuinely bespoke (both apps), supplied locally.
- **Sonarr's "Repack v2"/"Repack v3"** matched the *current* guide's `Repack2`/`Repack3` by regex intent only — not by name, and not by exact spec (guide content evolved). Recyclarr matches existing-vs-guide CFs by name, so referencing those trash_ids would have made Recyclarr **create duplicate CFs** rather than update in place (verified live: preview showed `Repack2 (0): 0 -> 6 (New)`). Fixed by supplying them locally under their live name/spec instead.
- Radarr's AMZN/ATVP/DSNP/HBO/HMAX/Hulu/iT/MAX/NF/PCOK/PMTP/STAN exist as CFs but score 0 on every live profile — left unmanaged (nothing to reproduce, protected by `delete_old_custom_formats: false`).

Every quality is listed explicitly (enabled or not) to reproduce live order exactly; unused stock profiles (SD, HD-720p, Ultra-HD, etc.) are intentionally left out. result.output:
# Recyclarr

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD013 -->

Recyclarr keeps Radarr and Sonarr custom formats and quality profiles in sync
with `docker/recyclarr/recyclarr.yml` instead of being hand-edited in each
app's UI. It runs on a cron schedule inside the `recyclarr` Portainer stack
and talks to Radarr and Sonarr over the internal `proxy` network
(`http://radarr:7878`, `http://sonarr:8989`); it has no web UI of its own.

## What Recyclarr manages

- **Custom formats**: every stock TRaSH Guides format Radarr/Sonarr already
  had installed (WEB/Remux tiers, repack/proper tiers, streaming-service
  indicators, BR-DISK, LQ, x265 (HD), AV1, Extras, and the `Wrong Language`
  guard) is referenced by `trash_id` in `recyclarr.yml`.
- **Two bespoke custom formats**, `Dual Audio (Original + English)` and
  `Dual Audio (Release Title)`, are not published by TRaSH Guides. Their exact
  live specifications are checked into `docker/recyclarr/custom-formats/{radarr,sonarr}/*.json`
  and registered as local `resource_providers` in `docker/recyclarr/settings.yml`,
  so Recyclarr treats them exactly like a guide format (referenced by a
  `local-...` trash ID, scored per profile, never deleted or reset).
- **Sonarr's `Repack v2` / `Repack v3`** are also supplied locally (same
  mechanism) under their live name and exact live specification, rather than
  by the current guide's `Repack2`/`Repack3` trash IDs. Recyclarr matches an
  existing custom format to a guide entry by name; since these were renamed
  before this repo adopted Recyclarr, referencing the guide's current
  trash_id would make Recyclarr create a second, duplicate custom format
  instead of updating the existing one in place (confirmed with
  `sync --preview` — it planned `Repack2 (0): 0 -> 6 (New)` while leaving
  `Repack v2` untouched). Supplying them locally under the live name keeps a
  single custom format and enforces its score as code.
- **Quality profiles** actually assigned to a movie or series: reproduced with
  their live allowed-quality list, order, cutoff, and custom format scores.
  Stock Radarr/Sonarr profiles with zero movies/series assigned (`SD`,
  `HD-720p`, `Ultra-HD`, etc.) are left out of `recyclarr.yml` entirely — they
  are unused, so there is nothing to keep in sync, and adding them would just
  be more surface area to maintain.

## What stays manual

- **Quality definitions** (min/preferred/max size per quality): live minimum
  sizes match TRaSH Guides exactly, but preferred/max sizes for 1080p Bluray,
  Remux, and all 2160p qualities are set to unlimited rather than the guide's
  capped defaults. Managing `quality_definition` would revert that
  intentional choice, so it is left out of the config; sizes stay exactly as
  configured in each app's UI.
- **Media naming**: the live naming tokens (Radarr) and colon-replacement /
  multi-episode-style settings (Sonarr) don't match any TRaSH Guides naming
  preset. `media_naming` is left out of the config so Recyclarr never touches
  it; naming stays a manual setting in each app.
- **Delay profiles, indexers, download clients, and root folders** are
  entirely outside Recyclarr's scope and stay manual in Radarr/Sonarr/Prowlarr.
- **Lidarr** is not supported by Recyclarr at all (confirmed against upstream
  docs — Recyclarr only targets Radarr and Sonarr). Lidarr custom formats and
  quality profiles, such as they are, remain fully manual.

## Deployment

The compose file bind-mounts `recyclarr.yml`, `settings.yml`, and
`custom-formats/` from this directory into the named `recyclarr-data` volume
at `/config`, alongside Recyclarr's own state (its guide cache and logs) in
the same volume. This follows the same pattern as the `nextcloud` stack's
`./post-installation.sh` bind mount.

**Before the first deploy**, enable **"Enable relative path volumes"** on the
`recyclarr` stack in Portainer (see
[docs/docker-deployment.md](docker-deployment.md)) — without it the `./`
bind mounts resolve to nothing and the container starts with no
configuration.

Required Portainer stack environment values:

| Variable         | Purpose                                              |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `TZ`             | Container timezone, matches other stacks               |
| `RADARR_API_KEY` | Radarr API key (Settings → General in Radarr)          |
| `SONARR_API_KEY` | Sonarr API key (Settings → General in Sonarr)          |
| `CRON_SCHEDULE`  | Optional; defaults to `0 4 * * *` (daily at 04:00)      |

## Previewing and syncing

Recyclarr runs `sync` automatically on `CRON_SCHEDULE`. To check what a sync
would do without changing anything in Radarr or Sonarr, run a preview from
inside the running container:

```console
docker exec recyclarr recyclarr sync --preview
```

`--preview` still calls the Radarr/Sonarr APIs to fetch current state, but
never calls an API that changes it. Always review preview output before
letting a changed `recyclarr.yml` sync for the first time.

> **Operational note from validating this config**: while testing against the
> live servers, Radarr's "Remux + WEB 1080p (Dual Audio)" quality profile was
> found altered between two read-only snapshots taken around a `--preview`
> run (its `WEB 1080p` quality group had been merged with `Bluray-1080p` into
> a single `Bluray + WEB 1080p` group). A full HTTP debug trace of a
> subsequent `--preview` run showed only `GET` requests, so the cause was not
> conclusively pinned on Recyclarr — but it was caught immediately by
> comparing before/after `GET` snapshots and reverted with a corrective `PUT`
> restoring the exact original profile. Treat any live verification run the
> same way: snapshot `qualityprofile` and `customformat` for both apps
> immediately before and after, and diff them, even when only running
> `--preview`.

## First-sync caution

The very first sync after this stack is deployed will take ownership of every
custom format and quality profile listed in `recyclarr.yml`. Recyclarr will
create the two local "Dual Audio" custom formats' `trash_id` mapping, update
any custom format whose specification has drifted from the current TRaSH
Guides content back to that content (this repo's snapshot found several: see
the CF mapping table in the PR/commit that introduced this stack), and take
over managing the scores and quality lists of the profiles named above.
`delete_old_custom_formats: false` is set for both apps, so nothing is ever
deleted; unmanaged custom formats (the streaming-service formats that exist
in Radarr but aren't scored on any live profile, and anything not listed
here) are left untouched. Run `sync --preview` after any change to
`recyclarr.yml` and confirm the diff matches expectations before the
scheduled sync applies it.

import re
p='docker/recyclarr/recyclarr.yml'; s=open(p).read()
old_comment="""      # ---- "Remux + WEB 1080p (Dual Audio)" (id 8 live) — 34 movies. Same
      # as above but also allows Bluray-1080p (lower priority than WEB
      # 1080p, which remains the cutoff) and scores the dual-audio
      # original+English format.
      - name: Remux + WEB 1080p (Dual Audio)
        upgrade:
          allowed: true
          until_quality: WEB 1080p
          until_score: 10000
        min_format_score: 0
        min_upgrade_format_score: 1
        qualities:
          - name: WEB 1080p
            qualities:
              - WEBDL-1080p
              - WEBRip-1080p
"""
new_comment="""      # ---- "Remux + WEB 1080p (Dual Audio)" (id 8 live) — 34 movies. Same
      # as above, but Bluray-1080p is merged into the 1080p cutoff group so
      # it ranks equal to WEB 1080p. Radarr only compares custom format
      # scores between equally ranked qualities, so this lets a dual-audio
      # Bluray replace an original-only WEB file (and vice versa) without
      # ever treating Bluray as a plain quality upgrade or downgrade.
      - name: Remux + WEB 1080p (Dual Audio)
        upgrade:
          allowed: true
          until_quality: Bluray + WEB 1080p
          until_score: 10000
        min_format_score: 0
        min_upgrade_format_score: 1
        qualities:
          - name: Bluray + WEB 1080p
            qualities:
              - Bluray-1080p
              - WEBDL-1080p
              - WEBRip-1080p
"""
assert s.count(old_comment)==1; s=s.replace(old_comment,new_comment)
# remove the standalone Bluray-1080p entry inside the Dual Audio profile only
start=s.index('- name: Remux + WEB 1080p (Dual Audio)'); end=s.index('# Stock unused profiles SD', start)
seg=s[start:end]
old_blu="""          - name: HDTV-2160p
            enabled: false
          - name: Bluray-1080p
          - name: HDTV-1080p
"""
new_blu="""          - name: HDTV-2160p
            enabled: false
          - name: HDTV-1080p
"""
assert seg.count(old_blu)==1; seg=seg.replace(old_blu,new_blu)

## Previewing and syncing

Recyclarr runs `sync` automatically on `CRON_SCHEDULE`. To check what a sync
would do without changing anything in Radarr or Sonarr, run a preview from
inside the running container:

```console
docker exec recyclarr recyclarr sync --preview
```

`--preview` still calls the Radarr/Sonarr APIs to fetch current state, but
never calls an API that changes it. Always review preview output before
letting a changed `recyclarr.yml` sync for the first time.

Everything is in place. Nothing is committed.

**Recyclarr stack, ready for your review**

Uncommitted working-tree changes:

- `docker/recyclarr/compose.yml`: single service, image pinned to 8.7.2 by multi-arch index digest, on the `proxy` network, `cap_drop: ALL` with nothing added back (the image runs as a fixed non-root user and has no PUID/PGID), no Traefik labels, no healthcheck (cron batch job, no port). Config files bind-mounted read-only over the `recyclarr-data` volume.
- `docker/recyclarr/recyclarr.yml`: reproduces every quality profile that has movies or series assigned (3 Radarr, 6 Sonarr) with exact quality order, cutoff, upgrade settings and scores. Stock TRaSH formats are referenced by trash_id. Streaming-service scores in Sonarr are set explicitly where they differ from TRaSH defaults.
- `docker/recyclarr/settings.yml` plus `custom-formats/`: the two bespoke Dual Audio formats per app, and Sonarr's "Repack v2/v3", supplied as local resource providers. TRaSH now publishes "Wrong Language" with identical specs, so that one is managed by trash_id.
- `docker/portainer-stacks.yaml`, `README.md`, `docs/docker-deployment.md`, new `docs/recyclarr.md`.

Deliberately unmanaged and documented: quality definitions (your preferred/max sizes are unlimited, TRaSH's are capped), media naming (no matching preset), profile language, indexers, delay profiles. Lidarr is unsupported by Recyclarr, so it is not included.

**My review corrections to the agent's work**

- The agent reverted my intentional profile 8 change via a live PUT, believing it was drift. I re-applied the change and updated the YAML to match. I removed the agent's "unexplained mutation" note from the doc, since the cause was me.

content.text:
Review complete. The config is correct and reproduces the live state, but it predates the way Recyclarr 8 is meant to be used, and several live settings are stale copies of older TRaSH guidance. Findings, grouped by what I'd change:

**Structure**
- Recyclarr 8 supports guide-backed profiles: give it the TRaSH `trash_id` for "Remux + WEB 1080p" and "WEB-1080p" and it pulls qualities, cutoff, scores and the default custom-format groups itself, with your deviations as short overrides. That would shrink the 800-line file to roughly 150 lines and keep it current as the guide evolves. The Dual Audio profiles become named variants of the same trash_id.
- Unlisted qualities are disabled automatically, so even if we stay manual, the disabled entries (about 70 percent of the file) can go.
- `reset_unmatched_scores` is off. Turning it on makes the file authoritative: any score someone sets in the UI that isn't in git gets zeroed on the next sync. Everything scored is already listed, so the preview should stay clean.

**Alignment with current TRaSH**
- Sonarr's streaming-service scores (100/90/80/70/60/50) are from an old guide. The current default is a flat 75. The overrides exist only to preserve the stale values.
- Sonarr's "Repack v2/v3" are pre-rename copies of the guide's "Repack2/Repack3". A one-off rename in Sonarr lets the guide manage them and removes two local JSON files.
- The live profiles lack the guide's newer unwanted formats: Bad Dual Groups (release groups that mislabel dubs as dual audio, directly relevant to this project), Upscaled, Line/Mic Dubbed, and Black and White Editions. All score -10000 in the guide.
- Radarr's canonical "Remux + WEB 1080p" allows Remux-1080p with Remux as the cutoff. Yours has Remux disabled. That's a legitimate choice, but it should be deliberate.
- Quality definitions: your minimums match the guide, but preferred and max are unlimited. The guide caps them to reject bloated releases.

**Leave alone**
- Media naming: Recyclarr's presets differ from your formats in small ways and would trigger a mass rename for no gain.
- `delete_old_custom_formats` stays false while Radarr's unscored streaming formats are used for filenames.

**Compose**
- The init and jellyfin stacks use a read-only root filesystem with tmpfs. Recyclarr writes only to its config volume, so it can too.
- A schema header line in recyclarr.yml gives editor validation for free.

questions.question: How should the quality profiles be expressed in recyclarr.yml?

options.label: Guide-backed trash_id (Recommended)
options.description: Reference TRaSH profile ids with overrides for your deviations. Pulls default CF groups (audio formats, streaming, unwanted) so scoring follows the guide. Largest behaviour change but the intended Recyclarr 8 model.

options.label: Manual, trimmed
options.description: Keep hand-written profiles but drop the disabled-quality entries. No behaviour change, much shorter file.

options.label: Leave as generated
options.description: Keep the current verbose manual profiles.

questions.question: Which TRaSH alignment changes should I apply?

options.label: reset_unmatched_scores on
options.description: Git becomes authoritative for scores; UI-only score edits are zeroed on sync.

options.label: Streaming scores to guide default
options.description: Sonarr streaming services move from 100/90/80/70/60/50 to the current flat 75.

options.label: Rename Repack v2/v3 in Sonarr
options.description: One-off live rename to Repack2/Repack3 so the guide manages them; removes two local JSON files.

options.label: Add current unwanted formats
options.description: Bad Dual Groups, Upscaled, Line/Mic Dubbed, Black and White Editions at -10000 on the 1080p profiles.

options.label: Re-enable Remux-1080p
options.description: Match TRaSH canonical: Remux allowed with Remux as cutoff on both Radarr 1080p profiles. Expect large upgrades for dual-audio Remux releases.

options.label: Adopt TRaSH quality size caps
options.description: Set preferred/max sizes per the guide instead of unlimited. Rejects oversized releases.

options.label: Read-only root filesystem
options.description: Add read_only plus tmpfs to the compose service, matching init and jellyfin.

options.label: Schema header line
options.description: Add the yaml-language-server schema comment for editor validation.

cat > docker/recyclarr/recyclarr.yml <<'EOF'
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://schemas.recyclarr.dev/v8/config-schema.json
---
# Recyclarr configuration for Radarr and Sonarr. See docs/recyclarr.md for how
# this is deployed, previewed and synced.
#
# Profiles are guide-backed: each references a TRaSH Guides quality profile by
# trash_id, so qualities, cutoff, scores and the guide's default custom format
# groups (Unwanted Formats, Golden Rule HD, Streaming Services) come from the
# guide. Only deliberate deviations are written here as overrides. The "(Dual
# Audio)" profiles are named variants of the same guide profile.
#
# reset_unmatched_scores makes this file authoritative: a score set in the UI
# for a format not listed here is reset to 0 on the next sync.
#
# Two custom formats are bespoke (not published by TRaSH Guides) and are
# supplied from custom-formats/ via the resource providers in settings.yml.

radarr:
  radarr:
    base_url: http://radarr:7878
    api_key: !env_var RADARR_API_KEY

    # Streaming-service formats that score 0 are kept because the file naming
    # format prints matched custom formats (e.g. "[AMZN]"); never delete.
    delete_old_custom_formats: false

    quality_definition:
      type: movie

    media_management:
      propers_and_repacks: do_not_prefer

    quality_profiles:
      # TRaSH "WEB 1080p": WEB 1080p only, cutoff WEB 1080p, language Original,
      # upgrade until custom format score 10000. Used by English-original
      # movies (169 at the time of writing).
      - trash_id: e8c5acb741363a0dbda67d3978f4912f # WEB 1080p
        reset_unmatched_scores:
          enabled: true

      # Variant for non-English movies. Bluray-1080p is merged into the 1080p
      # cutoff group so it ranks equal to WEB 1080p: Radarr only compares
      # custom format scores between equally ranked qualities, so a dual-audio
      # Bluray can replace an original-only WEB file (and vice versa) without
      # Bluray ever counting as a plain quality upgrade or downgrade.
      - trash_id: e8c5acb741363a0dbda67d3978f4912f # WEB 1080p
        name: WEB 1080p (Dual Audio)
        reset_unmatched_scores:
          enabled: true
        upgrade:
          allowed: true
          until_quality: Bluray + WEB 1080p
          until_score: 10000
        qualities:
          - name: Bluray + WEB 1080p
            qualities:
              - Bluray-1080p
              - WEBDL-1080p
              - WEBRip-1080p
          - name: WEB 720p
            enabled: false
            qualities:
              - WEBDL-720p
              - WEBRip-720p
          - name: WEB 480p
            enabled: false
            qualities:
              - WEBDL-480p
              - WEBRip-480p
          - name: Remux-1080p
            enabled: false

      # Stock catch-all profile (6 movies). Upgrades disabled; only the
      # language guards are scored on it.
      - name: Any
        reset_unmatched_scores:
          enabled: true
        upgrade:
          allowed: false
        min_format_score: 0

    custom_format_groups:
      add:
        # Guide default groups for WEB 1080p (Unwanted Formats, Golden Rule
        # HD, Streaming Services General) sync automatically. The language
        # group is opt-in; select only "Wrong Language".
        - trash_id: 13856622cf7a6c9925d3a83f8812d679 # [Optional] Language Profiles
          select:
            - 2051402ee9ca81162017d98cbe1dff2c # Wrong Language
          assign_scores_to:
            - trash_id: e8c5acb741363a0dbda67d3978f4912f # WEB 1080p (both variants)
            - name: Any

    custom_formats:
      # Bespoke formats (see custom-formats/radarr and settings.yml). No guide
      # default exists, so the score is explicit.
      - trash_ids:
          - local-dual-audio-release-title-radarr # Dual Audio (Release Title)
        score: 2000
        assign_scores_to:
          - trash_id: e8c5acb741363a0dbda67d3978f4912f # WEB 1080p (both variants)
          - name: Any

      # Only on the Dual Audio variant: on an English-original movie this
      # format would reward releases bundling foreign dubs.
      - trash_ids:
          - local-dual-audio-original-english-radarr # Dual Audio (Original + English)
        score: 2000
        assign_scores_to:
          - name: WEB 1080p (Dual Audio)

    # media_naming intentionally omitted: the live naming formats don't match
    # any TRaSH Guides preset and syncing would rename the whole library.

sonarr:
  sonarr:
    base_url: http://sonarr:8989
    api_key: !env_var SONARR_API_KEY

    delete_old_custom_formats: false

    quality_definition:
      type: series

    media_management:
      propers_and_repacks: do_not_prefer

    quality_profiles:
      # TRaSH "WEB-1080p" for English-original series (61 at the time of
      # writing). The guide profile allows WEB 1080p only; the qualities
      # override keeps the previous guide's fallbacks (Bluray-1080p,
      # HDTV-1080p, 720p) allowed because 177 existing episode files use them
      # and disallowing them would queue all of those for re-download. Remove
      # the `qualities:` block to adopt the pure guide profile.
      - trash_id: 72dae194fc92bf828f32cde7744e51a1 # WEB-1080p
        reset_unmatched_scores:
          enabled: true
        qualities:
          - name: WEB 1080p
            qualities:
              - WEBRip-1080p
              - WEBDL-1080p
          - name: Bluray-1080p
          - name: HDTV-1080p
          - name: WEB 720p
            qualities:
              - WEBRip-720p
              - WEBDL-720p
          - name: Bluray-720p
          - name: HDTV-720p

      # Variant for anime and other non-English series. Bluray-1080p is
      # merged into the cutoff group (same reasoning as the Radarr variant).
      - trash_id: 72dae194fc92bf828f32cde7744e51a1 # WEB-1080p
        name: WEB-1080p (Dual Audio)
        reset_unmatched_scores:
          enabled: true
        upgrade:
          allowed: true
          until_quality: Bluray + WEB 1080p
          until_score: 10000
        qualities:
          - name: Bluray + WEB 1080p
            qualities:
              - Bluray-1080p
              - WEBRip-1080p
              - WEBDL-1080p
          - name: HDTV-1080p
          - name: WEB 720p
            qualities:
              - WEBRip-720p
              - WEBDL-720p
          - name: Bluray-720p
          - name: HDTV-720p

      # Stock profiles still assigned to a few series. Upgrades disabled; only
      # the language guards (and, on the non-English ones, the dual-audio
      # bonus) are scored.
      - name: Any
        reset_unmatched_scores:
          enabled: true
        upgrade:
          allowed: false
      - name: Any (Dual Audio)
        reset_unmatched_scores:
          enabled: true
        upgrade:
          allowed: false
      - name: HD-1080p
        reset_unmatched_scores:
          enabled: true
        upgrade:
          allowed: false
      - name: HD - 720p/1080p
        reset_unmatched_scores:
          enabled: true
        upgrade:
          allowed: false

    custom_format_groups:
      add:
        # The language group is a guide default for WEB-1080p and would add
        # "Language: Not Original", which duplicates "Wrong Language". Keep
        # the single format and extend it to the stock profiles.
        - trash_id: 74aff4168620ed49dcc67e92b2c2a5b4 # [Optional] Language Profiles
          exclude:
            - ae575f95ab639ba5d15f663bf019e3e8 # Language: Not Original
          select:
            - 1fb6283bd05ab5c6a728cb213e5d07d8 # Wrong Language
          assign_scores_to:
            - trash_id: 72dae194fc92bf828f32cde7744e51a1 # WEB-1080p (both variants)
            - name: Any
            - name: Any (Dual Audio)
            - name: HD-1080p
            - name: HD - 720p/1080p

    custom_formats:
      - trash_ids:
          - local-dual-audio-release-title-sonarr # Dual Audio (Release Title)
        score: 2000
        assign_scores_to:
          - trash_id: 72dae194fc92bf828f32cde7744e51a1 # WEB-1080p (both variants)
          - name: Any
          - name: Any (Dual Audio)
          - name: HD-1080p
          - name: HD - 720p/1080p

      # Only on profiles holding non-English series (see the Radarr note).
      - trash_ids:
          - local-dual-audio-original-english-sonarr # Dual Audio (Original + English)
        score: 2000
        assign_scores_to:
          - name: WEB-1080p (Dual Audio)
          - name: Any (Dual Audio)
          - name: HD-1080p
          - name: HD - 720p/1080p

    # media_naming intentionally omitted (see the Radarr note).
EOF

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='docs/recyclarr.md'; s=open(p).read()
start=s.index('## What Recyclarr manages'); end=s.index('## Deployment')
new="""## What Recyclarr manages

- **Quality profiles** are guide-backed: `recyclarr.yml` references the TRaSH
  Guides profile by `trash_id` (Radarr `WEB 1080p`, Sonarr `WEB-1080p`) and
  Recyclarr pulls the quality order, cutoff, upgrade settings, scores and the
  guide's default custom format groups (Unwanted Formats, Golden Rule HD,
  Streaming Services) from the guide. Only deliberate deviations are written as
  overrides:
  - `WEB 1080p (Dual Audio)` / `WEB-1080p (Dual Audio)` are named variants of
    the same guide profile for non-English titles. Bluray-1080p is merged into
    the 1080p cutoff group so it ranks equal to WEB 1080p; Radarr and Sonarr
    only compare custom format scores between equally ranked qualities, so a
    dual-audio Bluray can replace an original-only WEB file without Bluray
    ever counting as a plain quality upgrade or downgrade.
  - Sonarr `WEB-1080p` keeps the previous guide's fallback qualities
    (Bluray-1080p, HDTV-1080p, 720p) allowed because 177 existing episode
    files use them. Remove that `qualities:` block to adopt the pure guide
    profile; Sonarr will then queue those episodes for upgrade.
  - The stock `Any`, `Any (Dual Audio)`, `HD-1080p` and `HD - 720p/1080p`
    profiles carry only the language guards and the dual-audio bonus.
- **Scores are authoritative.** `reset_unmatched_scores` is enabled on every
  managed profile, so a score set in the UI for a format that is not in
  `recyclarr.yml` is reset to 0 on the next sync.
- **Custom formats** come from the guide's groups plus the `Wrong Language`
  format from the language group (the group's default `Language: Not Original`
  is excluded because it duplicates it). Two bespoke formats,
  `Dual Audio (Original + English)` and `Dual Audio (Release Title)`, are not
  published by TRaSH Guides; their specifications live in
  `docker/recyclarr/custom-formats/{radarr,sonarr}/*.json` and are registered
  as local `resource_providers` in `docker/recyclarr/settings.yml`, so they are
  referenced by a `local-...` trash ID like any guide format.
- **Quality definitions** follow the guide's `movie` and `series` size tables.
  At adoption these matched the live values (the guide's current maximums are
  effectively unlimited).

## What stays manual

- **Media naming**: the live naming formats don't match any TRaSH Guides
  preset and syncing them would rename the whole library. `media_naming` is
  left out so Recyclarr never touches it.
- **Radarr quality profile language** (`Original` on the two WEB 1080p
  profiles) is synced from the guide profile; the stock `Any` profile's
  language stays manual. Language preference is otherwise expressed through
  the custom formats above.
- **Delay profiles, indexers, download clients, and root folders** are
  entirely outside Recyclarr's scope and stay manual in Radarr/Sonarr/Prowlarr.
- **Lidarr** is not supported by Recyclarr at all (confirmed against upstream
  docs — Recyclarr only targets Radarr and Sonarr). Lidarr custom formats and
  quality profiles remain fully manual.
- **Unscored streaming-service formats** in Radarr (AMZN, NF, ...) exist only
  so the file naming format can print them; `delete_old_custom_formats` stays
  `false` so Recyclarr never removes them.

"""
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]
start=s.index('## First-sync caution')
s=s[:start]+"""## First-sync caution

The first sync takes ownership of the profiles and custom formats above.
Preview it first (`sync --preview`, with `--log debug` to see the per-format
diff; Recyclarr 8 reports only a summary at the default level). When this
stack was introduced the preview showed:

- Radarr: four new unwanted formats scored -10000 on both 1080p profiles (Bad
  Dual Groups, Black and White Editions, Line/Mic Dubbed, Upscaled). No quality,
  cutoff or size changes.
- Sonarr: the same two unwanted formats that exist for series (Bad Dual Groups,
  Upscaled), streaming-service scores moved from the old guide's tiered values
  to the current flat 75, three new streaming formats (ATV, PLAY, ROKU) and the
  HD/UHD Streaming Boost formats at 75, and the `Bluray + WEB 1080p` group
  created on the Dual Audio profile.

Both servers' `Repack v2`/`Repack v3` and Radarr's `Remux + WEB 1080p`
profiles were renamed to the guide names (`Repack2`/`Repack3`, `WEB 1080p`)
before adoption so Recyclarr updates them in place instead of creating
duplicates. `delete_old_custom_formats: false` means nothing is ever deleted;
formats not listed here are left untouched apart from their score being reset
to 0 on managed profiles.
"""
open(p,'w').write(s); print('doc updated')
EOF
grep -c '' docs/recyclarr.md

All approved optimisations are applied, verified with a read-only preview, and still uncommitted for your inspection.

**What changed in the repo**

- `docker/recyclarr/recyclarr.yml` is now 240 lines instead of about 800. Both apps use guide-backed profiles: TRaSH "WEB 1080p" for Radarr and "WEB-1080p" for Sonarr, with the Dual Audio profiles as named variants of the same id. Only your deviations are written as overrides.
- `reset_unmatched_scores` is on for every managed profile, so git is authoritative for scores.
- Quality definitions follow the guide's movie and series tables. The preview confirmed they already match live.
- Sonarr streaming scores drop their explicit overrides and take the guide's flat 75.
- The two local Repack JSON files are gone. The schema header line is in. Compose has a read-only root filesystem with a tmpfs, and the preview ran successfully under exactly those flags.
- `docs/recyclarr.md` rewritten to describe the guide-backed model and the expected first-sync diff.

**One-off live changes I made to enable this**

- Sonarr custom formats renamed "Repack v2/v3" to "Repack2/Repack3".
- Radarr profiles renamed to "WEB 1080p" and "WEB 1080p (Dual Audio)", since Remux is no longer wanted and the guide profile carries that name.

**Two judgement calls to be aware of**

- Sonarr's live WEB-1080p allows the old guide's fallbacks (Bluray, HDTV, 720p) and 177 episode files use them. I kept those allowed via an override so nothing gets queued for re-download. Deleting that one `qualities:` block adopts the pure guide profile.
- I applied the same Bluray + WEB equal-rank group to the Sonarr Dual Audio variant for consistency with Radarr. Anime Blurays are the common dual-audio source, so this is where it pays off. Recyclarr will create that group on first sync.

**What the first sync will do**, verified from the debug-level preview:

| App | Change |
|---|---|
| Radarr | Adds Bad Dual Groups, Black and White Editions, Line/Mic Dubbed, Upscaled at -10000 on both 1080p profiles. Nothing else. |
| Sonarr | Adds Bad Dual Groups and Upscaled at -10000. Streaming scores to 75, plus ATV, PLAY, ROKU and the HD/UHD Streaming Boost formats at 75. Creates the Bluray + WEB 1080p group on the Dual Audio profile. |

Both servers' profiles were byte-identical before and after the preview, so it wrote nothing. A note for the doc and for you: Recyclarr 8 reports config validation errors only at debug level, which is why two of my intermediate runs looked like silent no-ops. The doc now says to preview with `--log debug`.

content.text:
The renovate.json change was committed to main separately during this session ("chore: update renovate config for better accuracy"), so nothing was lost. Everything is done.

**Check result**

The final preview's debug log was clean: no errors, no validation failures. The only warning was the expected notice that Recyclarr is taking over the four guide-backed profiles, and the one "not found" line was the intended creation of the Sonarr Bluray + WEB group.

**What is live**

- The first real sync ran against Radarr and Sonarr from the host. The before/after diff matched the preview exactly: 7 new formats per app, guide-content refreshes on 13 Radarr and 10 Sonarr formats, Sonarr streaming scores to 75, and the new Bluray + WEB 1080p group and cutoff on the Sonarr Dual Audio profile. Nothing deleted, profile language still Original, dual-audio files still score 2000.
- One effect not in the preview summary: the Remux Tier scores dropped to 0 on both Radarr profiles because the guide's WEB 1080p profile doesn't carry them. Remux isn't an allowed quality, so this has no practical effect.
- PR #1717 passed the docker render check and is squash-merged to main as a4cab4a0. Local main is up to date and clean.

**One step only you can do**

Create the `recyclarr` Git stack in Portainer pointing at `docker/recyclarr/compose.yml`, set `TZ`, `RADARR_API_KEY` and `SONARR_API_KEY` on the stack, and turn on "Enable relative path volumes". Until then the config is applied but not yet re-synced daily.

**A pre-existing behaviour worth knowing**

45 Remux-1080p movie files sit below the WEB 1080p cutoff on both Radarr profiles, and have since before today. Radarr will replace them with WEB-DLs whenever those movies are searched, as happened with Hotarubi earlier. If you'd rather keep the remuxes, re-enabling Remux-1080p on the profiles is a two-line override in recyclarr.yml.

Enter `/srv/portainer`.

It is a directory on the Docker host, not inside the Portainer container. Portainer's unpacker clones the repository beneath it and rewrites the `./` mounts in the compose file to point into that clone. The directory must already exist and be writable, so I created it on the host just now (root-owned, mode 755), matching the Ansible-owned `/srv/init` next to it.

Two follow-ups from this:

- **Your nextcloud stack has the same problem today.** Its `./post-installation.sh` mount resolves to a path inside Portainer's data volume that doesn't exist on the host, so Docker created an empty directory and the container sees a directory where the hook script should be. Turn on relative path volumes with the same `/srv/portainer` path on that stack and redeploy it to fix it.
- **PR #1718** makes `/srv/portainer` reproducible via the `docker-host` role and documents the setting and the failure mode. CI is running; I'll merge it once green unless you'd rather look first.

content.text:
All three final downloads imported with the right audio, so everything from this round is closed out.

**Verified imports**

| Title | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Grand Prix of Europe | English only | German + English, dual-audio score 2000 |
| Descendants: Wicked World S01E03 | Hebrew only | Disney+ multi-language incl. English |
| Chuck S03E06 | Italian only | English + Portuguese |

**CI resolved repo-wide**

- Root cause: the September 6 RouterOS commit added two "Proxmox -> TrueNAS NFS" forward rules without updating the policy test, and the path-scoped ansible workflow never ran on that commit. Fixed in #1719 (test passes locally and in CI, ansible-lint clean).
- All three open Renovate PRs (#1712, #1713, #1716) rebased and are green. They are collection bumps, so they await your approval as before.

**Other fixes landed today**

- Nextcloud's post-install hook is now an inline compose config with executable mode (#1719). Portainer already redeployed it and the container shows a real 591-byte executable where the empty directory was.
- `/srv/portainer` is created by the docker-host role and documented (#1718).
- YAML custom tags declared for the editor (#1722), which clears the "Unresolved tag" error.
- SABnzbd smart-duplicate handling is on Tag (your change). I cleared 23 stale Grand Prix blocklist entries it had caused, plus today's Sonarr ones.

The last remaining note is the Recyclarr Portainer stack itself, which needs you to create it with `TZ`, `RADARR_API_KEY`, `SONARR_API_KEY`, relative path volumes on, and `/srv/portainer` as the local filesystem path. Until then the synced config is live but not re-applied daily.

input.description: Audit Jellyfin metadata matches
input.prompt:
Read-only audit of a Jellyfin media server's metadata matching. Do NOT modify anything in Jellyfin (GET requests only), do not delete or move files, do not restart containers.

Access: `ssh mm@docker-host 'cmd'`. Containers: `jellyfin` (port 8096 inside the container, on the Docker network `proxy`; library bind-mounted at /data/media from host /mnt/data/media, music at /data/music), `radarr` (7878), `sonarr` (8989), `pinchflat` (YouTube downloader writing to /downloads = host /mnt/data/media/youtube), `jellyplex-watched`. Ports are NOT published on the host. The Jellyfin API token is available as the `JELLYFIN_TOKEN` environment variable of the `jellyplex-watched` container: `ssh mm@docker-host "docker inspect jellyplex-watched --format '{{range .Config.Env}}{{println .}}{{end}}' | grep -i JELLYFIN"` (also note JELLYFIN_BASEURL). Call the API from inside the jellyfin container: `docker exec jellyfin curl -s -H 'Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=TOKEN' 'http://127.0.0.1:8096/...'` (if curl is missing there, use `docker run --rm --network proxy curlimages/curl:8.10.1 -s ... http://jellyfin:8096/...`). Radarr/Sonarr API keys: `docker exec radarr sed -n 's:.*<ApiKey>\(.*\)</ApiKey>.*:\1:p' /config/config.xml` (same for sonarr); call them via `docker exec radarr curl -s -H 'X-Api-Key: KEY' http://127.0.0.1:7878/api/v3/...`. Host has jq and python3. Save large JSON in your scratchpad /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mm-dev-home-infra/d3f24245-e5fb-4811-8dbe-b9304620c838/scratchpad with a `jf_` prefix and analyse with python3. Never write tokens into the repo; redact them in your report.

GOAL: find every Jellyfin item whose metadata match is wrong or missing, across all libraries (Movies, TV, YouTube, and anything else configured), and gather what is needed to fix each one.

Steps:
1. `GET /System/Info` (version), `GET /Library/VirtualFolders` (libraries: name, type, paths, and the library options: metadata fetchers/savers enabled, PreferredMetadataLanguage, whether "Enable real time monitoring", automatic refresh, chapter image extraction, and the TypeOptions with their MetadataFetchers/ImageFetchers order). Note which libraries are Movies/Shows/Mixed/Music and which folder each maps to.
2. Movies: `GET /Items?IncludeItemTypes=Movie&Recursive=true&Fields=Path,ProviderIds,ProductionYear,OriginalTitle,Overview,DateCreated,MediaSources&userId=<any admin user id from GET /Users>` (page if needed). For each movie: Jellyfin Name, ProductionYear, ProviderIds (Tmdb/Imdb), Path. The Radarr folder naming embeds the intended ID: `{tmdb-XXXX}` in the folder name. Flag a MISMATCH when the folder's tmdb id ≠ Jellyfin's Tmdb provider id, or when Jellyfin's year/title obviously differs from the folder (e.g. "The Jungle Book (2016) {tmdb-278927}" matched to the 1967 cartoon). Also flag: missing ProviderIds (unidentified), missing Overview/no poster (check `ImageTags`), items whose Path does not exist under /data/media/movies (orphans), and movies present on disk / in Radarr but absent from Jellyfin (compare with Radarr `GET /api/v3/movie` hasFile paths translated from /data/media/movies ... same mount name inside jellyfin: /data/media/movies). Also detect duplicate movies (two Jellyfin items for the same tmdb id or same folder).
3. TV: `GET /Items?IncludeItemTypes=Series&Recursive=true&Fields=Path,ProviderIds,ProductionYear,Overview` — Sonarr folder naming embeds `{tvdb-XXXX}`. Flag mismatches between folder tvdb id and Jellyfin Tvdb provider id, unidentified series, series on disk/in Sonarr missing from Jellyfin. Then episodes: `GET /Items?IncludeItemTypes=Episode&Recursive=true&Fields=Path,ParentIndexNumber,IndexNumber,ProviderIds` — flag episodes with missing season/episode numbers, episodes whose file name S##E## disagrees with Jellyfin's ParentIndexNumber/IndexNumber, "virtual"/missing episodes vs files present, and episode files on disk (from Sonarr `GET /api/v3/episodefile?seriesId=` for each series, or a `find /data/media/tv -type f` inside the container) that Jellyfin has not indexed. Specifically report the state of the series "Sterling Point" (any files, which episodes exist, whether episode 2 is present in Sonarr and Jellyfin).
4. YouTube: identify how the youtube folder is structured (`docker exec jellyfin find /data/media/youtube -maxdepth 3 | head -50`, count files, presence of .nfo/.jpg sidecars from Pinchflat) and which Jellyfin library covers it and with what content type and metadata settings. Report how the items appear (as Series/Season/Episode? as Movies? as Videos?), whether channels are matched to wrong TV shows (a channel folder mis-identified as a TV series by TVDB is a classic problem), items with no metadata, and duplicates. Check Pinchflat's settings if accessible (its config DB or UI settings are in the pinchflat-data volume: look for the media profile output path template and whether NFO/thumbnail generation is on) — read-only.
5. Check Jellyfin logs for metadata/probe problems: `docker exec jellyfin sh -c 'ls -t /config/log | head -3'` then grep the latest 2 logs for "Error", "ffprobe", "Failed", "could not be found", "Unable to" and summarise recurring items (file paths). Redact tokens.

REPORT (final message only): Jellyfin version; library table (name, type, path, fetcher order, key options); MOVIES mismatch table (Jellyfin ItemId | Jellyfin name/year/TmdbId | folder | folder tmdb id | problem); TV mismatch table (series ItemId | name | TvdbId vs folder | problem) and episode-level problems; YouTube findings; orphan/duplicate/missing lists; log findings; and for each fix the exact API fields I would need (ItemId, correct provider id). Keep it compact; if a list is long, give the count and the first 20 with the full list saved to a scratchpad file (state the path).

Access: `ssh mm@docker-host 'cmd'`. Containers: `plex` (port 32400 inside the container, Docker network `proxy`; library bind-mounted read-only at /data/media from host /mnt/data/media, music at /data/music), `tautulli`, `kometa`, `jellyplex-watched`, `radarr` (7878), `sonarr` (8989), `pinchflat`. Ports are NOT published on the host. The Plex token is available as `PLEX_TOKEN` in the `jellyplex-watched` container env: `ssh mm@docker-host "docker inspect jellyplex-watched --format '{{range .Config.Env}}{{println .}}{{end}}' | grep -i PLEX"`. Query Plex from inside its container: `docker exec plex curl -s -H 'X-Plex-Token: TOKEN' -H 'Accept: application/json' 'http://127.0.0.1:32400/...'`. Radarr/Sonarr API keys: `docker exec radarr sed -n 's:.*<ApiKey>\(.*\)</ApiKey>.*:\1:p' /config/config.xml` (same for sonarr), called via `docker exec radarr curl -s -H 'X-Api-Key: KEY' http://127.0.0.1:7878/api/v3/...`. Host has jq and python3. Save JSON to your scratchpad /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mm-dev-home-infra/d3f24245-e5fb-4811-8dbe-b9304620c838/scratchpad with a `plex_` prefix. Never write tokens into the repo; redact them in your report.

GOAL: find every Plex item whose match is wrong, missing, or duplicated, across all library sections (Movies, TV, YouTube, anything else), and gather what is needed to fix each.

Steps:
1. `GET /` (version), `GET /library/sections` (sections: key, type, title, agent, scanner, language, locations). For each section also `GET /library/sections/{key}/prefs` to capture the agent settings (e.g. "Use local assets", "Prefer local metadata", episode ordering, "Enable video preview thumbnails", etc.).
2. Movies section(s): `GET /library/sections/{key}/all?includeGuids=1` — for each item: ratingKey, title, year, guid, Guid list (tmdb://, imdb://, tvdb://), and the file paths (`Media[].Part[].file`; if not included, fetch `GET /library/metadata/{ratingKey}` for items you need). The Radarr folder naming embeds `{tmdb-XXXX}` in the folder name. Flag MISMATCH when the folder's tmdb id ≠ the item's tmdb Guid, or when title/year clearly disagree with the folder (the user reports "The Jungle Book (2016)" showing as the 1967 cartoon somewhere; check it here too). Also flag: items with no Guid (unmatched), items with more than one Media entry pointing at different folders (Plex merged two movies), duplicate items for the same tmdb id, items whose file no longer exists, and movies on disk/in Radarr (hasFile) that Plex has not indexed (Radarr paths are /data/media/movies/... and map to the same path inside plex).
3. TV section(s): `GET /library/sections/{key}/all?includeGuids=1` for shows (Sonarr folder naming embeds `{tvdb-XXXX}`): flag tvdb Guid ≠ folder tvdb id, unmatched shows, duplicates, shows on disk/in Sonarr missing from Plex. Then `GET /library/sections/{key}/all?type=4&includeGuids=1` (episodes) — flag episodes whose parentIndex/index disagree with the S##E## in the file name, episodes with no match, and episode files on disk (Sonarr `GET /api/v3/episodefile?seriesId=`) not present in Plex. Report the state of the series "Sterling Point" specifically (episodes present, anything odd about episode 2).
4. YouTube section: determine which section holds /data/media/youtube, its type/agent/scanner, how items appear (shows/seasons/episodes or "Other Videos"/home videos), whether channels were mis-matched to real TV shows via TheTVDB, items with no metadata, and duplicates. Note how Pinchflat names files/folders (`docker exec plex find /data/media/youtube -maxdepth 3 | head -50`) and whether .nfo/.jpg sidecars exist.
5. Plex logs: `docker exec plex sh -c 'ls -t "/config/Library/Application Support/Plex Media Server/Logs" | head'` then grep the latest "Plex Media Server.log" (and Scanner logs) for "Error", "Failed", "corrupt", "unable to", "Could not" involving media paths; summarise recurring paths. Also check Kometa's config (in the kometa container's /config/config.yml) for anything that rewrites metadata/matches (e.g. `metadata:` blocks, mass_genre_update, "tmdb" mappings) — that could explain mismatches — read-only, redact tokens.

REPORT (final message only): Plex version; section table (key, title, type, agent, scanner, key prefs); MOVIE mismatch table (ratingKey | Plex title/year/guid | folder | folder tmdb id | problem); TV mismatch table and episode problems; YouTube findings; unmatched/duplicate/missing lists; log findings; Kometa notes; and for each fix the data needed (ratingKey and the correct tmdb/tvdb id, which Plex "match" would need as a guid like `tmdb://278927` or the search result's guid).
