input.description: Audit media file integrity
input.prompt:
Read-only integrity audit of a media library. Do NOT delete, move, rename or modify any file; do not change Radarr/Sonarr (GET only); do not restart containers. Be considerate of the host: it is a live media server on NFS storage, so limit ffprobe concurrency to about 4 parallel processes and do NOT fully decode files (no `ffmpeg -f null` over whole files).

Access: `ssh mm@docker-host 'cmd'`. Library on the host: /mnt/data/media/{movies,tv,youtube,...} (NFS). The `jellyfin` container mounts it at /data/media and has ffprobe at /usr/lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/ffprobe (use `docker exec jellyfin /usr/lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/ffprobe ...`). Radarr (7878) and Sonarr (8989) containers mount it at /data/media as well; their API keys: `docker exec radarr sed -n 's:.*<ApiKey>\(.*\)</ApiKey>.*:\1:p' /config/config.xml` (same for sonarr); call `docker exec radarr curl -s -H 'X-Api-Key: KEY' http://127.0.0.1:7878/api/v3/...`. Host has jq, python3. Scratchpad for your files: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mm-dev-home-infra/d3f24245-e5fb-4811-8dbe-b9304620c838/scratchpad (prefix `integ_`). Note: Radarr is currently downloading replacements for ~30 movies (Remux files being replaced by WEB-DL); files under /data/media/movies may change while you scan — record timestamps and don't treat a just-replaced file as an anomaly. Redact API keys in your report.

GOAL: find broken, truncated, corrupt, zero-length, or otherwise unplayable media files, plus files the download managers don't know about (orphans) and library entries whose files are missing, across movies, TV and YouTube. The user reports that "Sterling Point" episode 2 was corrupt (they may have deleted it since).

Method:
1. Inventory: `docker exec jellyfin find /data/media -type f \( -iname '*.mkv' -o -iname '*.mp4' -o -iname '*.avi' -o -iname '*.m4v' -o -iname '*.webm' -o -iname '*.ts' -o -iname '*.mov' \) -printf '%s\t%TY-%Tm-%Td\t%p\n'` → save the list; counts per top-level folder; total size. Flag zero-length and suspiciously small files (< 20 MB for movies/tv episodes, < 1 MB for youtube). Also list leftover junk: .part/.!qB/.tmp/.nzb/.par2/sample files, empty directories, and directories under movies/tv with no video file.
2. Header/container check with ffprobe on EVERY video file (this only reads headers, it's cheap): `ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration,size,bit_rate:stream=index,codec_type,codec_name -of json FILE`. Record: exit code, stderr (errors like "moov atom not found", "Invalid data found", "EBML header parsing failed"), duration, whether there is at least one video and one audio stream. Run with about 4-way parallelism (xargs -P4) inside the jellyfin container; write results as JSONL in the scratchpad. Files where ffprobe fails, or duration is missing/0, or no video/audio stream → BROKEN candidates.
3. Truncation check for MKV/MP4: a truncated download usually still has a valid header but a duration much shorter than expected, or an MKV without a Cues/duration element. Compare ffprobe duration against the expected runtime: Radarr `GET /api/v3/movie` → `runtime` (minutes) per movie (match by path), Sonarr `GET /api/v3/series` → `runtime` per series and `GET /api/v3/episodefile?seriesId=` → `mediaInfo.runTime`. Flag files whose duration is < 70% of the expected runtime (allow for specials/shorts; report the ratio). For files with no expected runtime, flag durations under 5 minutes in movies/tv.
4. Tail check for the BROKEN/truncated candidates only (not everything): `ffprobe -v error -read_intervals "99%" -show_entries frame=pkt_pts_time -of csv FILE 2>&1 | tail -3` or `ffmpeg -v error -sseek near end -t 10 -i FILE -f null -` limited to the last ~20 seconds, to confirm whether the file end is readable. Keep this to the candidate list.
5. Consistency with Radarr/Sonarr: movies: files on disk not referenced by any Radarr movieFile (orphans) and Radarr movieFiles whose path does not exist; TV: same via Sonarr episodefile paths; also Sonarr episodes with `hasFile: true` whose file is missing and series/episodes marked missing in Sonarr that are wanted (specifically "Sterling Point": list its episodes, hasFile, monitored, and any episodeFile entries and their mediaInfo). YouTube: report counts per channel folder, files with no matching .info.json/.nfo/.jpg sidecar if Pinchflat writes them, and any ffprobe failures.
6. Check Sonarr/Radarr history for past "import failed"/"corrupt"/"unable to parse mediainfo" events: `GET /api/v3/history?page=1&pageSize=200&eventType=...` or filter on `data.message` containing "corrupt", "MediaInfo", "failed" over the last 90 days; and both apps' `GET /api/v3/health` warnings.

REPORT (final message only): totals (files, size per folder); BROKEN list (path | size | ffprobe error | duration vs expected | Radarr/Sonarr id); TRUNCATED/short list; zero-length/junk/empty-dir list; orphans and missing-file lists (counts + first 20, full lists in scratchpad files, state paths); Sterling Point status; history/health findings; and any observation about how the corrupt files got there (e.g. failed usenet repair, partial imports). `/data/media/youtube/shows/<Channel>/Season <year>/s<year>e<uploadseq> - <title>.{mp4,nfo,jpg-thumb}` — one "season" per calendar year, episode number derived from upload date sequence. input.prompt:
You are adding an automated media-file integrity checker to the git repo at /Users/mm/dev/home-infra so that corrupt downloads are detected and re-downloaded automatically in future. DO NOT `git commit`, `git push`, `git add`, or switch branches (the user has their own branch checked out; leave the working tree changes uncommitted for review). Do not deploy anything to the Docker host; do not modify Radarr/Sonarr (GET only); read-only on the host apart from a dry-run described below.

## Context
- Docker host: `ssh mm@docker-host 'cmd'`. Media library on host /mnt/data/media/{movies,tv,youtube}; the `radarr` (port 7878), `sonarr` (8989) and `jellyfin` containers mount it at /data/media; all on the external Docker network `proxy`; ports not published (use `docker exec <ctr> curl ...`). Radarr/Sonarr API keys: `docker exec radarr sed -n 's:.*<ApiKey>\(.*\)</ApiKey>.*:\1:p' /config/config.xml` (same for sonarr). Never write API keys into the repo.
- Motivating incident: an episode file (Sonarr, WEB-DL MKV, 3.1 GB) imported cleanly but had ~18 Matroska structural errors ("invalid as first byte of an EBML number") scattered through the file body. A header-only `ffprobe` passed; only a full packet-level demux (`ffmpeg -v error -i FILE -c copy -f null -`, no decode) surfaced the errors. Radarr/Sonarr do not detect this. The tool must therefore be able to do a demux-level (or decode-level) check, not just ffprobe headers.
- Repo conventions you MUST follow: read README.md "Docker Services" (stack table, conventions), docs/docker-deployment.md (Portainer GitOps owns stacks in docker/portainer-stacks.yaml; env values/secrets live on the Portainer stack; stacks needing files from the repo use relative bind mounts with Portainer "relative path volumes" and Local filesystem path /srv/portainer — see docker/recyclarr as the freshest example, including its compose hardening: security_opt no-new-privileges, cap_drop ALL, read_only root fs + tmpfs where possible, digest-pinned image `image: repo:tag@sha256:...` (get the multi-arch index digest with `ssh mm@docker-host "docker buildx imagetools inspect IMAGE:TAG"`), healthcheck if sensible, restart unless-stopped), docs/docker-hardening.md, docs/recyclarr.md (doc style). CI runs `docker compose config` on docker/**; render-check your compose on the host with dummy env values (never real keys) in /tmp and clean up.

## Task
1. Research (web) the current options for automated corruption detection integrated with Radarr/Sonarr: Checkrr (github.com/aetaric/checkrr) first — confirm its current version, image (ghcr.io/aetaric/checkrr or docker hub), how it checks files (ffprobe only? does it run a full ffmpeg demux/decode? what do `ffprobe`/`ffmpeg` options in its config do), whether it keeps a database of already-checked files so subsequent runs only test new files, its schedule/cron config, its Radarr/Sonarr integration (does it delete the bad file, mark it failed/blocklist and trigger a re-search? via which API calls), whether config values can come from environment variables (Viper env binding, `${VAR}` substitution, or a secrets mechanism) since API keys must not be in git, and its resource footprint on a 4.4 TB NFS library. Also briefly evaluate at least one alternative (e.g. a Sonarr/Radarr Custom Script on import that runs `ffmpeg -c copy -f null` and marks the download failed via API; or another maintained tool) and state which you chose and why. Prefer the option that (a) catches demux-level corruption like the incident, (b) checks every new import promptly (within a day) and periodically re-checks, (c) re-downloads automatically via Radarr/Sonarr, (d) keeps secrets out of git.
2. Implement it as a new Portainer stack `docker/checkrr/` (or the chosen tool's name): compose.yml (hardened per conventions; mounts /mnt/data/media read-only at /data/media so paths match Radarr/Sonarr; joins `proxy`; a named volume for its state DB; resource limits or `nice`/low priority if the tool supports it so NFS isn't hammered — e.g. limit to 1-2 concurrent checks), the tool's config file(s) checked into the stack directory referencing env vars for `RADARR_API_KEY`/`SONARR_API_KEY`, and register the stack in docker/portainer-stacks.yaml, the README stack table, and a short docs/<tool>.md (what it checks, how it reacts to a corrupt file, schedule, required Portainer env values, relative-path setting, how to run a one-off scan and read its report). Scope the scan to /data/media/movies and /data/media/tv (YouTube files are not managed by Radarr/Sonarr; include youtube only in "report-only" mode if the tool supports per-path behaviour, otherwise leave it out and say so). Make sure a corrupt file is deleted only when the tool can hand the re-download to Radarr/Sonarr; never delete otherwise.
3. Dry-run validation on the host, read-only: `docker run --rm` the image with your config (keys passed as env vars from the host, config in /tmp) against a SMALL path (e.g. a single series folder such as "/data/media/tv/Sterling Point (2026) {tvdb-459552}" mounted read-only) in a mode that does NOT delete or call Radarr/Sonarr write APIs (dry-run/report-only if supported; otherwise omit the Radarr/Sonarr sections for the dry run). Confirm it runs, produces a report, and show how long a 3 GB file takes to check. Clean up /tmp afterwards. Run `docker compose config` on your compose file.

## Report (final message)
Files created/modified with a short description; tool + version + digest and how obtained; how the tool detects corruption and whether it would have caught the incident (cite docs/source); what happens on a corrupt file end-to-end; the schedule; secrets handling; dry-run output summary and timing; open questions for the human before first deploy. Redact keys.

cd /Users/mm/dev/home-infra-media && cat > docs/media-metadata.md <<'EOF'
# Media metadata and library integrity

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD013 -->

How Radarr, Sonarr, Jellyfin and Plex agree on what a file is, and how broken
files are caught. These settings live in the applications (Docker volumes),
not in Git, so this page is the record of the intended state.

## Identity flows from the download managers

- Radarr and Sonarr name folders with the provider id (`{tmdb-…}` for movies,
  `{tvdb-…}` for series) and write Kodi/Emby NFO sidecars with the same ids
  (Settings → Metadata → Kodi (XBMC) / Emby, metadata on, images off). The
  media servers read those ids instead of guessing from titles, which is what
  produced "The Jungle Book (2016)" matched to the 1967 cartoon.
- Both apps have Connect notifications to Plex and Jellyfin with "Update
  Library" on for import, upgrade, rename and delete, so the affected folder is
  rescanned immediately. NFS does not deliver inotify events, so this is the
  primary trigger; Plex additionally runs a scheduled scan every six hours.

## Jellyfin

| Library | Type | Path | Metadata |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Movies | movies | `/data/media/movies` | NFO first, then TheMovieDb and OMDb (internet providers on) |
| TV | tvshows | `/data/media/tv` | NFO first, then TheTVDB, TheMovieDb, OMDb (internet providers on) |
| YouTube | tvshows | `/data/media/youtube/shows` | NFO only (internet providers off) |
| Music | music | `/data/music` | MusicBrainz and TheAudioDB |

Internet providers must stay off for YouTube: Pinchflat writes `tvshow.nfo`
and per-video NFOs with a `youtube` unique id, and any online provider will
match a channel name to an unrelated TV series (Boundary became the anime
"Beyond the Boundary"). Channel items must carry only the `youtube` id.

The TheTVDB plugin is installed because TheMovieDb has no episode titles for
several series (One Piece, talk shows). When titles are missing after a
provider change, refresh the series with "Replace all metadata"; a plain
refresh keeps the existing placeholder name.

## Plex

| Section | Type | Agent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Movies | movie | Plex Movie | honours `{tmdb-…}` in folder names |
| TV | show | Plex TV Series | aired order |
| YouTube | show (hidden) | Plex NFO Series | one show per channel folder, seasons flattened |
| Music | artist (hidden) | Plex Music | |

The YouTube section must use the NFO agent. With the online TV agent every
channel's videos were pooled into one show because Pinchflat's date-based
episode numbers collide across channels. Changing the agent on an existing
section does not split the pooled show; the section had to be deleted and
re-created (watched state comes back from Jellyfin via jellyplex-watched).

Unmatched movies (`local://` guid) are usually new imports the agent has not
matched yet; "Refresh metadata" on the item matches it from the folder id.

## File integrity

Radarr and Sonarr validate only container headers on import. A 3 GB episode
with Matroska structural errors scattered through its body imported cleanly
and only failed a full demux pass:

```console
ffmpeg -v error -i FILE -c copy -f null -
```

The `checkrr` stack (see [docs/checkrr.md](checkrr.md)) runs that class of
check on new files and hands corrupt ones back to Radarr or Sonarr for
re-download. To fix one by hand: delete the episode or movie file in the app,
mark the grab as failed in History (this blocklists the release) and search
again, then re-run the demux check on the replacement.

## Jellyfin container mounts

Music is mounted once, at `/data/music`, which is the library path. An
earlier duplicate mount of `/mnt/music` at `/data/media/music` was nested
inside the read-only media bind and depended on an empty `music/` directory
existing on the NFS share; when that directory disappeared the container could
not start after a restart. Keep nested bind mounts out of read-only binds.
EOF

The Bluray copy of Beauty and the Beast is downloading with a watcher on it, and that's the last open item on the media side. Here is where everything stands, plus one question.

**Fixed today**

- Jellyfin: internet metadata providers enabled for Movies and TV, TheTVDB plugin installed and made the primary TV source, four mis-identified movies corrected (Jungle Book 2016, The Imaginary, Ratatouille, Scarlet), five YouTube channels stripped of bogus TV-show ids, all missing episode titles resolved (the remaining "Episode N" names are TheTVDB's real titles).
- Plex: seven unmatched movies matched, four stale file references fixed, Star Wars: Visions S2 episodes matched, periodic scans enabled every six hours, YouTube library rebuilt with the NFO agent: 12 channels, 286 of 286 videos, no merged episodes.
- Radarr and Sonarr now write NFO sidecars with TMDB and TVDB ids for every file, so both servers identify from the id rather than the title.
- Sterling Point S01E02: the corruption was in the FLUX release itself. Both indexer copies are blocklisted and a playWEB copy passes a full demux check, indexed in both servers.
- Remux downgrade: library is 1,253 GB, down from 1,788 GB. Remaining Remuxes are Coraline (no WEB release exists) and two dual-audio anime titles kept deliberately.

**One incident, resolved.** My Jellyfin restart exposed a fragile compose mount: a duplicate music bind nested inside the read-only media bind needed an empty directory on the NFS share that no longer existed, so the container couldn't start. I recreated the directory and Jellyfin was down for about six minutes. The redundant mount is removed in the pending change.

**Your call on the PR.** You denied the step that would move the Checkrr files out of your working tree. Right now the Checkrr stack (`docker/checkrr/`, `docs/checkrr.md`, README and stack-list edits) sits uncommitted on your `fix-cg13` checkout, and a separate worktree at `../home-infra-media` holds the media-metadata doc, the Jellyfin compose fix and its README link. Tell me whether to commit the Checkrr files from your tree into that branch, or leave them for you to commit yourself.

    image: aetaric/checkrr:3.6.1@sha256:c817e081e9397c240e5b13b09363fe26c9f94248489d3b4f0279e67495b1f12e
    container_name: checkrr
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    # Upstream's image has no non-root user, so this runs as root; cap_drop
    # ALL, no-new-privileges and a read-only root filesystem contain it. The
    # only writable paths are the checkrr-data volume and the /tmp tmpfs; the
    # media library is bind-mounted read-only. See docs/checkrr.md.
    cap_drop:
      - ALL
    read_only: true
    tmpfs:
      - /tmp
    networks:
      - proxy
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ}
      - RADARR_API_KEY=${RADARR_API_KEY}
      - SONARR_API_KEY=${SONARR_API_KEY}
    # Checkrr has no env-var config support, so the entrypoint renders the
    # template with the API keys into tmpfs at start (docs/checkrr.md).
    entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "/config/entrypoint.sh"]
    volumes:
      - checkrr-data:/data
      - ./checkrr.yaml.tpl:/config/checkrr.yaml.tpl:ro
      - ./checkrr-entrypoint.sh:/config/entrypoint.sh:ro
      - type: bind
        source: /mnt/data/media
        target: /data/media
        read_only: true
        bind:

    # Checkrr checks one file at a time; these limits cap ffmpeg's CPU/RAM
    # during a full decode pass so other containers and the NFS server are
    # not starved, and cpu_shares yields to every other container.
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:

          memory: 1g
    cpu_shares: 512
    # No healthcheck: cron-scheduled batch job with no listening port.
    restart: unless-stopped
'''
